scope: fenced dispatch, backend circuit breaking, host lock, and exact Docker resource reconciliation

checks.name: queue and dispatcher unit suite
checks.command: uv run --locked --project lab --python 3.12.14 python -m unittest lab.tests.test_queue lab.tests.test_automation_dispatcher -v
coverage: expired fenced lease remains interrupted until cleanup is confirmed
cleanup=false quarantines the run and blocks claim resumption
backend unavailable opens the circuit immediately
three successful half-open sentinels close the circuit
Linux cross-process host lock excludes a second controller
Docker reconciliation only removes exact campaign/job/attempt/generation labels

checks.name: live Docker label reconciliation injection
checks.command: sg docker -c '<start two benign pinned-image containers; reconcile target labels; verify unrelated remains running; remove both test containers>'

implementation: SQLite queue uses per-attempt opaque fencing tokens and generation numbers; fenced lease expiry makes the run interrupted rather than auto-requeueing.
Lease renewal and result commit validate the active attempt token; retry is enabled only after positive cleanup reconciliation.
DockerWorker can label resources with campaign, job, attempt, and generation; reconciler verifies exact labels before force-removal and confirms no matching resource remains.
Backend circuit breaker stops new claims on daemon/API loss, cleanup uncertainty, or configured repeated failures; half-open dispatch is sentinel-only.
A host-local cross-process lock prevents concurrent controllers.
limitations: No Windows tests, Sandbox checks, or Windows host-lock execution were run.
The dispatcher is a callable single-host execution component; the campaign CLI does not yet expose end-to-end execute/resume commands.
No catalog plugin was installed or executed; this evidence does not change compatibility gates.
